title: Maximum Strength of a Group
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums representing student scores in an exam, determine the maximum product that can be obtained by multiplying the scores of a non-empty subset of these students.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums representing student scores in an exam, determine the maximum product that can be obtained by multiplying the scores of a non-empty subset of these students. The strength of a group of students is defined as the product of their scores.
constraints: Choose any nonempty index subset of nums.
Its strength is the product of its selected values.
Return the maximum possible strength, preserving duplicate indices as separate choices.
hints: Every positive value greater than zero can only improve a positive product.
Use all negatives when their count is even; when odd, discard the negative closest to zero.
If no nonzero product remains, choose zero when available, otherwise the largest negative singleton.
Two negatives multiply positively, and exchanging a retained negative for one with larger magnitude cannot decrease the resulting positive product.
editorial: Two negatives multiply positively, and exchanging a retained negative for one with larger magnitude cannot decrease the resulting positive product.

tests.explanation: Using all six values produces the positive maximum product 1350.
Choosing the two values -5 and -4 gives the maximum product twenty.
